# Do your package.json, .nvmrc, Dockerfile and CI agree on which Node.js to run?

> Paste package.json, .nvmrc, .tool-versions, a Dockerfile and a GitHub Actions workflow and see whether your Node.js versions drifted: a pin that breaks engines.node, majors that disagree across files, end-of-life Node.js, an unbounded engines range, or one no Node.js version satisfies. Free, deterministic, runs in your browser.

Free to use and source available (FSL-1.1-MIT). Results are estimates from the numbers typed in, not legal, tax, financial or professional advice.

## Source

- [Source code and README](https://github.com/duncan-haywood/oss-monorepo/tree/main/ventures/node-version-drift-check): FSL-1.1-MIT licensed.

## Verification

- The range parser is differential-tested against node-semver 7.7.4 (the library npm uses for engines.node): on 150,000 seeded random ranges, satisfies agreed on all 794,376 checks and overlap agreed on all 65,063 pairs of satisfiable ranges. Method and the known differences (prereleases read as releases; an unsatisfiable range never overlaps) are in the README.
